changes.text: 一克镭的市价是十万美元。而制备镭的方法，是她和丈夫皮埃尔·居里多年前毫无保留地公开的，镭工业正靠它发展起来、高价卖货。公开了方法的她，实验室里那点镭当时只用于为医院提取射气；后来为本书写引言的梅洛尼在美国发起募捐，希望借此让她把研究继续下去。这笔账，她在书里一项一项算过。

A gram of radium then sold for one hundred thousand dollars. The process for preparing it had been published years earlier, without reserve, by Marie Curie and her husband Pierre Curie, and the radium industry was now thriving on that very process and selling its product at a high price. She had helped give the method away, yet the radium in her laboratory was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use, and Meloney, who later wrote the book's introduction, set out to raise a subscription in America to enable her to go on with her work. In her book she worked through that account line by line.
居里夫妇把制备镭的方法毫无保留地公开，镭工业因此自由发展；他们自己却长期缺钱、缺场地。1921年赠镭之前，后来为本书写引言的梅洛尼去探访时，她的实验室仍设备不足；靠美国妇女募捐，居里夫人才得到一克镭。这是一笔两边都有分量的账。

The Curies published their method for preparing radium without reserve, and the radium industry grew freely on it. They themselves long went without money and without a proper workplace. When Meloney, who later wrote the book's introduction, visited before the 1921 gift, Marie Curie's laboratory still lacked sufficient equipment, and a subscription raised by American women finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands. It is a ledger with weight on both sides.
事情要从1890年代末的巴黎说起。居里夫妇要从矿石里提取镭和钋，可他们缺合适的工作场所、缺人手，也缺钱。沥青铀矿很贵，他们买不起足够的量。当时这种矿物的主要来源在波希米亚的圣约阿希姆斯塔尔，奥地利政府在那里经营一座提铀的矿。矿上的残渣还从没用过，他们相信镭和一部分钋就在残渣里。靠维也纳科学院的影响，他们以优惠价拿到几吨残渣。起初的费用出自自己的积蓄，后来才得到少量补助和一些外部帮助。

The story begins in Paris in the late 1890s. The Curies were trying to extract radium and polonium from ore, and they lacked a proper place to work in, personnel and money. Pitchblende was an expensive mineral, and they could not afford to buy a sufficient quantity. At that time the principal source of this mineral was at St. Joachimsthal in Bohemia, where the Austrian government worked a mine for the extraction of uranium. Its residues had so far not been used at all, and they believed the radium, and part of the polonium, would be found in them. Through the influence of the Vienna Academy of Sciences they secured several tons of the residues at an advantageous price. In the beginning the costs came out of their own pockets; only later were they given a few subventions and some help from outside sources.
化学处理只能在一间废弃的储藏室里做：木棚、沥青地面、玻璃屋顶挡不住雨，里面没有任何设施，只有几张破松木桌、一个不好使的铸铁炉和皮埃尔爱用的黑板。没有排气罩带走化学处理放出的毒气，活儿得搬到院子里做；天气不好的时候就在棚里接着干，把窗子开着。

The chemical treatments had to be carried on in an abandoned storeroom: a wooden shed with a bituminous floor and a glass roof that did not keep the rain out, and without any interior arrangements. All it contained were some worn pine tables, a cast-iron stove that worked badly, and the blackboard Pierre Curie loved to use. There were no hoods to carry away the poisonous gases thrown off by the treatments, so the work had to be moved outside into the court; when the weather was unfavorable they went on inside, leaving the windows open.

这时日内瓦方面来请皮埃尔：那里物质条件更好，还能过上近似乡居的宁静生活。按居里夫人的记述，这个决定很艰难，皮埃尔动了心。最后让他定下来不去的，是他们正对镭做的研究，他怕这样的变动打断它。此时，索邦为医科学生而设的P.C.N.物理教席正好空缺。他申请后，在一心想让他不必离开法国的庞加莱的影响下获聘；她则受托在塞夫尔的女子师范学校讲物理课。他们留在巴黎，收入增加了，工作却更难：皮埃尔要兼两处课，其中学生众多的P.C.N.教学让他非常疲惫。

Then Geneva came calling for Pierre, offering material advantages and the opportunity of a life comparable in its tranquillity with that in the country. In Marie Curie's account the decision was a grave one, and Pierre was tempted. What finally settled it was the radium research itself, since he feared the interruption that such a change must involve. At this moment the chair of physics in the Sorbonne's P.C.N. course was vacant; this was the physics, chemistry and natural history curriculum compulsory for medical students. He applied, and was appointed through the influence of Henri Poincaré, who was anxious to free him from the necessity of quitting France. Marie Curie was given charge of the physics lectures at the Normal School for Girls at Sèvres. They stayed in Paris and their income increased, but working conditions grew harder: Pierre was doing double teaching, and the P.C.N., with its very large number of students, fatigued him greatly.

新职位不带实验室。在索邦设于居维叶街12号、供P.C.N.教学用的附属楼里，他只有一间小办公室和一个工作间。他想接收学生做研究，就去争取更大的场地。照她的说法，做过这类事的人知道那是一堵怎样的墙：公文、登门、请求，有一点成果都要付出很多，这些事彻底让他厌倦和沮丧。除了这些困难，没有工业手段处理原料，研究也推不动。早在1899年，皮埃尔就借中央化学产品公司（他因制造天平与之有往来）的一处现成设施，组织了第一次工业试验，技术细节由德比埃尔纳安排得很成功，试验效果良好；这种需要特殊小心的活儿，还得专门训练人手。

The new post came without a laboratory. In the annex of the Sorbonne at 12 rue Cuvier, which served as teaching quarters for the P.C.N., all he had at his disposition was a little office and a single work room. He meant to receive students and start them in research, so he took steps to find larger working quarters. Anyone who has taken similar steps knows the wall of financial and administrative obstacles he was throwing himself against: the official letters, the visits, the requests, and what even the least success entailed. It all thoroughly wearied and discouraged him. Besides these difficulties, the research could not advance without industrial means of treating the raw material. As early as 1899 Pierre Curie organized a first industrial experiment, using for it a chance installation placed at his disposition by the Central Society of Chemical Products, with which he had dealt over the construction of his balances. The technical details were arranged very successfully by André Debierne, and the operations brought good results, though a special crew had to be trained for chemical work that demanded special precautions.

钱还是不够。受这次试验启发，法国实业家阿尔梅·德·利尔办起一座在当时看来很大胆的真正镭工厂，把产品卖给医生；医生们因各种研究的发表，已对镭的生物效应和可能的疗法产生兴趣。项目成功了，因为他能雇到居里夫妇训练过的人。镭从此有了稳定货源，价格很高：制备条件特殊，制镭所需矿物的价格又立刻上涨。德·利尔出于好意，在厂里给他们一小块工作地方和一部分费用。其余的钱有的是他们自己的，有的来自补助，最重要的一笔是1902年科学院给的20,000法郎。

The money was still short. Inspired by their attempt, a French industrialist, Armet de Lisle, took what seemed at that epoch the daring step of founding a veritable radium factory to furnish the product to physicians, whose interest in the biological effects of radium and its possible therapeutic applications had been aroused by the publication of various investigations. The project proved a success because he could employ men already trained by the Curies in the delicate processes of the manufacture. Radium was now regularly placed on sale, at a high price it is true, given the special conditions under which it had to be made and the immediate rise in the cost of the minerals necessary to its production. Armet de Lisle, in an entirely disinterested manner, placed a little working place in his factory at their disposition, together with a part of the means necessary to use it. Other funds were added either by the Curies themselves or through subventions, the most important of which, accorded by the Academy of Sciences in 1902, amounted to 20,000 francs.

据梅洛尼记述，仪式前一夜又出了岔子：文件要把这一克镭放在居里夫人个人名下。她读完说不行。这一克镭代表很多钱，可它更代表美国的妇女，不是给她的，是给科学的。她身体不好，随时可能死；女儿伊夫尚未成年，一旦她去世，镭就会进她的遗产，由两个女儿分掉。她要求当晚就把文件办好：第二天就要接收镭，而她可能明天就死，事关重大（据梅洛尼转述）。于是那个闷热的五月夜晚，虽然已经很晚，他们还是请到律师，照她自拟的草稿写好文件。她在动身去华盛顿前签了字：她死后，这一克镭归巴黎的镭研究所，供居里实验室专用。第二天在白宫，哈定总统交给她的是一把小金钥匙。

As Meloney tells it, on the eve of the ceremony there was one more snag: the papers were to put this gramme of radium in Marie Curie's own name. Marie Curie read them and said it must not be left that way. The gramme represented a great deal of money, but more than that it represented the women of the country: it was not for her, it was for science. She was not well and might die any day. Her daughter Eve was not of legal age, and if she died the radium would go into her estate and be divided between her daughters. That was not its purpose; it had to be consecrated for all time to the use of science. The paper had to be fixed that night, because the next day she received the radium, and, she said, as Meloney reports it, "I might die tomorrow. Too much is at stake." So, late as it was on that hot May evening, a lawyer was secured and prepared the paper from a draft Marie Curie herself had written. She signed it before starting for Washington: in the event of her death the gramme of radium went to the Institut du Radium in Paris, for the exclusive use of the Laboratoire Curie. The next day at the White House, what she received from President Harding was the small golden key.
作者提出另一种做法（书中没有写他们讨论过任何替代方案）：分用途授权，研究与教学免费，商业开发收费；或者只对产品收费，把方法留在公共领域。这条路或许能留下一点收入，代价是谈判、监督，以及与工业界的长期纠缠。朋友们主张的则是保留权利、用收益建研究所。作者认为，差别不在谁更高尚，而在谁承担风险。

The author's alternative, and the book records no such discussion: license by use, free for research and teaching and charged for commercial exploitation, or else charge for the product and leave the method in the public domain. Some income might have been kept that way, at the price of negotiation, oversight, and a long entanglement with industry. What the friends urged was retaining the rights and building the institute out of the proceeds. In the author's view, the difference is not who is nobler; it is who carries the risk.
边界要交代清楚：本篇的史实全部出自同一本书，1923年麦克米伦版《皮埃尔·居里》，C.与V.凯洛格英译。皮埃尔·居里传记和自传笔记都是居里夫人本人的叙述，梅洛尼那几段是她的转述，都不是独立记录。不申请专利的那个决定，书里没写日期，也没留下会议或对话的记录，本文不补写。

The limits need to be stated. Every historical fact in this piece comes from one book: Pierre Curie, Macmillan, 1923, translated by C. and V. Kellogg. The Pierre Curie biography and the autobiographical notes are Marie Curie's own account, and the Meloney passages are her report of what she saw and heard; none of it is an independent record. The decision not to patent is undated in the book, and no minutes or conversations of the deliberations survive there; this piece does not supply them.

dispositions.rationale: hook.1 中英均点明皮埃尔·居里是她的丈夫，并在梅洛尼首次出现处说明她是后来为本书写引言、在美国发起募捐的人；ev 补入 CUR-E11 以支持“丈夫”。

evidence.quote: My husband, as well as myself, always refused to draw from our discovery any material profit.
It was my hope when I arrived in New York, a few weeks afterwards, to find ten women to subscribe ten thousand dollars each

dispositions.rationale: 导语中英均在梅洛尼首次出现处加注“后来为本书写引言”，交代其身份。

evidence.quote: I also learned that Madame Curie's laboratory, although practically a new building, was without sufficient equipment

dispositions.rationale: 中文补上“和一些外部帮助”，与英文及原文一致。

evidence.quote: later we were given a few subventions and some help from outside sources

dispositions.rationale: 删去证据未写出的目标“提纯到能确认是新元素”，中英改为“要从矿石里提取镭和钋”。

evidence.quote: We believed that we would find all the radium and a part of the polonium in the residues of this mine
had as their objective the preparation of pure radium salts

dispositions.rationale: 中文补入“里面没有任何设施”，英文原样保留。

evidence.quote: a glass roof which did not keep the rain out, and without any interior arrangements

dispositions.rationale: 中文补入庞加莱一心想让他不必离开法国，英文原样保留。

evidence.quote: who was anxious to free him from the necessity of quitting France

dispositions.rationale: 把“同时/Meanwhile”改为“除了这些困难/Besides these difficulties”，并写明“早在1899年/As early as 1899”，不再暗示工业试验与索邦新职的困难同时发生。

evidence.quote: As early as 1899 Pierre Curie succeeded in organizing a first industrial experiment

dispositions.rationale: 中文补入该公司因制造天平与皮埃尔有往来，以及试验效果良好。

evidence.quote: with which he had had relations in connection with the construction of his balances

dispositions.rationale: 英文改为“the annex of the Sorbonne at 12 rue Cuvier”，与中文一致。

evidence.quote: in the annex (12 rue Cuvier) of the Sorbonne

dispositions.rationale: 中文补入办厂在当时看来很大胆，以及医生的兴趣由各种研究的发表引起。

evidence.quote: which seemed daring at that epoch
had been aroused by the publication of various investigations

dispositions.rationale: 中文“最大的一笔”改为“最重要的一笔”；同时把金额写作“20,000法郎”，与英文数字一致。

evidence.quote: of which the most important, accorded in 1902 by the Academy of Sciences, amounted to 20,000 francs

dispositions.rationale: 中文补入她可能明天就死、事关重大这一理由，并标明是梅洛尼转述；英文原样保留。

evidence.quote: To-morrow I receive the radium, and I might die tomorrow. Too much is at stake.

dispositions.rationale: 末句中英均标为作者的判断（作者认为/In the author's view）。
中英分别收窄为“本篇的史实/Every historical fact”，不再涵盖虚构场景和作者解释，并与 uncertainty_note 的说法一致。
